title: Advance Variation
intro: 3.e5: get the bishop out to f5, then ...e6 and ...c5 against White's pawn chain.

steps.text: White opens with 1.e4.
Play the Caro-Kann.
White takes the centre with 2.d4.
Challenge the centre.
steps.ifRight: e4 is attacked. White must push, exchange or defend.

steps.text: 3.e5 is the Advance Variation. White gains space and closes the centre.
Get your light-squared bishop out before ...e6 shuts it in.
steps.hint: The bishop on c8 can reach f5.
steps.ifWrong: 3...Bf5: the bishop leaves before ...e6 closes its diagonal.
steps.ifRight: Then ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6 attack White's pawn chain.

feedback.e7e6: 3...e6 shuts in your bishop on c8. Get it out first with 3...Bf5.
feedback.c6c5: 3...c5 is played too, but this repertoire develops the bishop first.

steps.text: Your bishop is outside the pawn chain. Now ...e6 will not shut it in.
Another order: 2.Nf3 d5 3.e5. Bring the bishop out before ...e6, with a pin.
steps.ifWrong: 3...Bg4 pins the knight and gets the bishop out before ...e6.

feedback.c8f5: 3...Bf5 is playable, but with the knight on f3, the pin with 3...Bg4 is stronger.

lessons.title: 4.Nf3: ...e6 and the plan
lessons.summary: Support d5, then attack the base of the chain.

steps.text: 4.Nf3 develops and protects d4.
Support d5 and free your dark-squared bishop.
steps.ifWrong: 4...e6 is safe now: your bishop is already out.
steps.ifRight: Next come ...c5 to hit d4, and the knights to d7 and e7.

steps.text: White's chain runs from d4 to e5. Your plan is ...c5, attacking its base on d4.
5.Be2 is a calm set-up. White gets ready to castle.
The plan stays the same: ...c5, then ...Nc6 and more pressure on d4.
Another order: 2.Nf3 d5 3.e5 Bg4 4.d4. Your bishop is out. Find the next move.
steps.ifWrong: 4...e6 is safe, because the bishop is already outside the chain.

lessons.title: 4.Bd3: trade, then ...c5
lessons.summary: Take the bishop trade, then hit d4.

steps.text: 4.Bd3 offers to trade light-squared bishops.
Take the trade.
steps.ifWrong: 4...Bxd3: without this bishop, White has one attacker less.
steps.ifRight: White takes back with the queen.

feedback.f5g6: 4...Bg6 lets White take on g6 and damage your pawns. Take on d3 yourself.

steps.text: 5.Qxd3 takes back.
Now ...e6 costs nothing. Play it.
steps.hint: Your bishop is gone, so the e-pawn can move freely.
steps.ifWrong: 5...e6: the bishop is already out and traded.

steps.text: 6.Nf3 develops and guards d4.
Hit the base of White's pawn chain.
steps.ifRight: Your queen and knights will add pressure on d4.

steps.text: Here White played 6.Ne2 instead of 6.Nf3. Find the same pawn strike.
steps.ifWrong: 6...c5 hits the base of the chain.
steps.ifRight: The plan does not depend on where White's knight goes.
